title: Min-cost sequence clustering batcher: kernel-aware, KV-local continuous batching
author: Riley Parker
description: Motivation: continuous batching in the runtime needs better cost-aware grouping to reduce padding waste while preserving kernel-friendly shapes and KV cache locality. Prior bucketing approaches reduced padding but treated every bucket as independent, which caused kernel underutilization and KV cache churn for mixed-length workloads. This PR implements a min-cost sequence clustering batcher that jointly optimizes for (1) padded-token cost, (2) kernel shape efficiency (selected kernel cost per batch shape), and (3) KV cache locality score to favor co-locating prefix-contiguous requests. The change is backward compatible: runtime batching policy is pluggable and defaults to previous bucketed batcher. Key pieces implemented: 1) Cost model module that combines padding penalty, kernel selection latency estimator, and a KV-locality penalty; weights are tunable via config. 2) New clustering-based batch composer that runs a lightweight greedy min-cost merge on the active queue every scheduling tick; it considers sequence-length centroids and merges neighboring clusters when cost(delta) < merge_threshold. 3) Kernel-aware batch shaping: after clusters are chosen the composer queries the kernel registry to pick an execution kernel optimized for the resulting max sequence length and batch size; cluster merges that would force a kernel downgrade are penalized. 4) KV cache affinity: requests with overlapping prefixes are annotated by the router and assigned a KV affinity token; the batcher prefers grouping identical affinity tokens to avoid cross-device KV synchronization. 5) Continuous batching tweaks: adaptive timer that backs off when clustering yield is low and aggressive coalescing for tail latencies. 6) Extensive unit and integration tests simulating mixed-length traffic and cold KV scenarios. Performance summary (brief): in internal synthetic workloads with bimodal seqlen (8/1024) we measured 22-28% token-cost reduction vs baseline bucketed batching at equivalent 95th percentile latency target; in a production trace sample with mixed web chat traffic we observed 11% reduction in GPU time and 14% fewer KV cache misses. Rollout plan: feature gated via runtime config; staged rollout to Dedicated clusters then Redwood-hosted starting with non-critical models. This PR also includes a small telemetry addition exposing batch cost breakdown per schedule tick for offline analysis.

diff_snippets:
+++ b/runtime/batcher/min_cost_clustering.py
+class MinCostClusterComposer:
+    def schedule(self, queue):
+        clusters = self._init_clusters(queue)
+        while True:
+            pair, delta = self._find_best_merge(clusters)
+            if delta >= self.merge_threshold:
+                break
+            self._merge(pair)
+        return self._materialize_batches(clusters)

+++ b/runtime/batcher/cost_model.py
+def estimate_cost(cluster):
+    padding_cost = cluster.size * (cluster.max_len - cluster.avg_len) * padding_weight
+    kernel_cost = kernel_registry.estimate(cluster.shape) * kernel_weight
+    kv_penalty = (1 - cluster.kv_locality_score) * kv_weight
+    return padding_cost + kernel_cost + kv_penalty

+++ b/runtime/kernel_registry/kernel_selector.py
+def estimate(batch_shape):
+    # return ms per token estimate for selected kernel path
+    if batch_shape.seq_len <= 64:
+        return L2_OPT_KERNEL_MS[token_class(batch_shape)]
review_comments:
Sophia Lin: Nice decomposition. Two asks: (1) add safety cap so merge loop can't starve the scheduler on high-concurrency queues, (2) add a simple A/B metric emitted when gating to compare cluster vs bucket for 1 week.
Response (Riley): added a hard cap on number of merges per tick and added 'batching.strategy_evaluation' telemetry event.

Mateo Ruiz: Kernel penalty weights look large in defaults and cause preference for tiny batches. Can you add auto-tune that nudges weights based on recent kernel throughput?
Response (Riley): added a light-weight exponential moving average tuner in cost_model with config switches (disabled by default).

Aria Chen: KV affinity token serialization in router is fine but ensure forward compatibility with on-prem affinity stores.
Response (Riley): switched token to a 128-bit stable hash and added compatibility shim in runtime/kv/affinity.rs.
performance_summary: Synthetic bimodal seqlen test: 22-28% token reduction vs bucketed baseline under same latency target. Production chat trace sample: 11% GPU time reduction, 14% fewer KV misses. Tail latency change within SLA (95th +3-6ms, within rollback window).
docs: docs/runtime/batching.md: new section 'Min-cost clustering batcher' with config knobs and rollout guidance
rollback_plan: Feature gated via 'batcher.strategy' config. Revert by switching to 'bucketed' strategy at runtime and optional restart of composer process. Emergency flag 'disable_clustering=true' added to config service.
release_notes: Introduces a new min-cost clustering batcher that reduces padding and KV cache churn for mixed-length workloads; feature off by default and gated for staged rollout. See docs/runtime/batching.md for config. Performance gains vary by workload.
notes_for_release_engineering: Enable feature gate per-cluster. Watch metrics: batch.cost_breakdown, runtime.kv_miss_rate, gpu_utilization. Start on canary Dedicated clusters before wider rollout.
pm_context: Linked ticket ENG-5215: optimize batching for mixed-length conversational workloads; ENG-5238: reduce KV churn for prefix-heavy routing.
